## Reading 4 ⭐ — `mergeable_state` reads the branch-protection surface that answers 403, 2026-09-21T18:29Z

Added because it was measured after this card was filed, and because it turned a stated NOT MEASURED into a
measurement without any new access.

### The gap

`GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/branches/main/protection` answers **403** 「Resource not accessible by
integration」 for this seat. Lit control on the same channel: `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack` → **200**.
⇒ the channel works and the protection surface specifically is closed. So 「is check X required?」 has no direct
instrument here.

### The indirect instrument

**`mergeable_state` on a non-draft PR is computed from that ruleset**, so reading it is an indirect read of the
surface the 403 hides:

| `mergeable_state` | what it says |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | a **required** check is failing or missing, or a required review is |
| `unstable` | mergeable, but a **non-required** check is failing |
| `clean` | nothing failing |

⚠️ **The PR must be out of draft.** A draft always reads `blocked`, which says nothing about requiredness — this
seat read `blocked` on a draft earlier today and it was draft state, ⛔ not a gate verdict.

### The measured instance

PR **#19616** carries a permanent, by-design red: `check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s DELIBERATE CORRECTION refusal,
which ⛔ no commit can clear. Out of draft, with that red final:

```
mergeable_state: unstable   mergeable: true   draft: false
```

⇒ `Check Changeset` is **not required**. Two independent readings agree, so the instrument is corroborated ⛔ not
trusted alone:

| instrument | reading |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` — the repo's own `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` | `Check Changeset` **absent**: grep exit 1, 0 lines. Lit control `Lint & Repo Gates`: **24** hits |
| the maintainer ruling on #18375 (`5729188290`, batch #158 item 1) | 「`Check Changeset` is **not** one of the seven `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, so its red is advisory and blocks nothing」 |

⭐ The three are not redundant. The registry is the repo's **declaration**; `check-required-contexts.mjs`'s own
header says the rename 「lands in two halves that CANNOT be atomic」 — this registry, and the entry in repository
Settings → Rulesets — so the registry can be right while Settings is stale. `mergeable_state` reads the **effect**
of Settings, which is the half the registry cannot speak for.

⇒ **the rule to write down**: when branch protection answers 403, do not report requiredness as unmeasurable.
Take the PR out of draft, let the checks settle, and read `mergeable_state`: `unstable` means the failing check is
advisory, `blocked` means it is not. ⛔ Never read it on a draft, and ⛔ never read it before the checks converge.

### ⚠️ And the trap that sits right next to it

「the red is advisory」 and 「this PR may land」 are **different propositions**. This seat had all three readings
above and was one act from arming #19616 — while the governing ruling required a confirmation channel the seat
had not satisfied at all. The measurement answers what blocks the *merge button*; it says nothing about what the
*process* owes. ⛔ Do not let a clean requiredness reading stand in for reading the ruling.

## ⛔ Correction to Reading 2 — the rule as filed is OVER-GENERAL and would mislead the next seat, 2026-09-21T18:45Z

Reading 2 in this card's body says the carrier reds `Check Changeset` for as long as it hangs on a
`Clause-②: no` PR. **That is true only in the case it was measured on.** A second measurement today
contradicts it, and the gate's own docblock says why.

### The contradicting measurement

PR **#19618** (`Clause-②: no`, carrier hung at 2026-09-21T18:27:33Z). `Check Changeset` on head
`7cc0ca1b3dc996a7e667cc90185ffdec2fd8559d`, both runs:

| started | result |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-09-21T18:24:23Z — before the carrier | **success** |
| 2026-09-21T18:27:37Z — **after** the carrier | **success** |

⇒ carrier present, declaration `no`, and the check is **green**. Under the rule as filed it should be red.

### The gate's own verdict table, which settles it

`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, the `judgeLevel` docblock, quoted:

> `clean` — the axis is CARRIED (`yes`, or `no (narrowing)`), and **no moved package is graded `patch`** → exit 0
> `discharged` — the axis is CARRIED, a moved package **IS graded `minor`+**, and others are graded `patch` → exit 0
> `enforce` — the axis is CARRIED, moved packages graded `patch` and **NONE of them graded `minor` or above** → exit 1

⇒ the carrier **carries the axis**; it is the **level** that decides the verdict. The refusal fires only when
every moved package is graded `patch`.

| PR | carrier | declaration | changeset levels | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #19595 | present | `no` | `@objectstack/spec`: **patch** (the only moved package) | `enforce` → **red** |
| #19618 | present | `no` | `spec`: **minor**, `metadata-core`: **minor**, `platform-objects`: patch | `discharged` → **green** |

### The rule, restated correctly

**Hanging `needs:contract-review` carries the clause-② axis. It reds `Check Changeset` only when every
package the PR moves is graded `patch`; a single `minor` or above on a moved package discharges it.**

⇒ what stays true from Reading 2: on a PR in the refusing shape the red is the **designed state**, ⛔ no commit
clears it, and it is ⛔ not a reason to withhold the strip. What was wrong is the claim that the carrier reds
**every** `Clause-②: no` PR.

### ⚠️ Where the wrong version went

This seat told **two** dispatched devs the over-general version — 「once the seat hangs that carrier your
`Check Changeset` goes RED」. On #19616 the check was indeed red, but for an unrelated reason (the
DELIBERATE CORRECTION refusal), so the instruction was **right by accident**; on #19618 it was simply wrong,
and the dev did not act on it either way. ⛔ Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because a rule filed on this
card is what the next seat reads instead of measuring.

⭐ The general shape of the error: the first measurement was a **crossed control on one PR** — same head, carrier
toggled, verdict flipped both ways — which is strong evidence that the carrier is *a* cause, and ⛔ no evidence
at all that it is a *sufficient* one. One PR cannot separate 「the carrier reds it」 from 「the carrier plus this
PR's level reds it」.

## ⛔ Correction to Reading 3 — its repair half was an INFERENCE presented as a measurement, and it is now measured, 2026-09-21T20:51Z

Reading 3 in this card's body states the footer divergence and then prescribes a repair, citing PR #19595's
body as the thing that carries it. **The failure half was measured; the repair half was not**, and the
citation does not do the work the sentence implies it does.

### What was wrong with the evidence, ⛔ not with the conclusion

| claim | status when filed |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /pulls` with a tail session-URL footer stores byte-identical, one footer | ✅ measured |
| `PATCH /pulls/{n}` with the same tail makes the platform append a second bare footer | ✅ measured |
| the repair (session attribution in prose, a **bare** footer under a rule line) survives a `PATCH` | ⚠️ **inferred** — and the cited evidence cannot support it |

⚠️ **Why the citation could not support it.** PR #19595's body was written once by `POST` and **never
`PATCH`ed**. So 「footer count 1」 on that body proves the repair shape *survives a create*. The claim it was
offered for is that the shape *stops a PATCH from appending*. ⇒ ⛔ different act, ⛔ different claim; the
evidence was **compatible** with the conclusion and was read as **support for** it.

### The measurement, taken now

PR **#19622**, body `PATCH` carrying the repair shape — prose attribution
(「Authored in Claude Code session `…` (`https://…`)」) plus a bare `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`
under a rule line:

```
sent   7320 bytes
stored 7320 bytes      delta 0
footers stored: 1
stored body is byte-identical to the sent body (prefix check: true)
```

⇒ **the repair shape holds on the `PATCH` path.** Reading 3's prescription stands; only its evidence
changes, from an inference to a reading.

### ⭐ The recurring error this is the third instance of today, named so it is findable

**Evidence being *compatible* with a claim read as evidence *supporting* it.** Compatibility needs one
example; support needs the competing explanations ruled out.

| instance | the compatible evidence | what it could not rule out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading 2 (corrected above) | one PR: same head, carrier toggled, verdict flipped both ways | that the level, not the carrier alone, was doing the refusing |
| the seat's claim on card #19578 | a `git grep` hit naming `protocol.zod.ts` | that the hit was an `import` line, not the declaration |
| Reading 3 (this correction) | PR #19595's body carries the repair shape with one footer | that the body had never been `PATCH`ed, so it tested the create path only |

⛔ All three were written as measurements. ⛔ None of the three conclusions turned out wrong, which is the
uncomfortable part: the habit produced correct answers three times and would not have announced itself if
the fourth had been wrong.

## Reading 5 — `check-issue-citations` is SURFACE-SCOPED, and this seat carried the unscoped version into four dispatch words, 2026-09-22T02:15Z

### The rule, read from the gate's own source

`scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs`:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| `CITATION_SURFACES` — what the gate **does** judge | `content/docs/releases/**/*.mdx` (whole-file), `packages/**/src/**/*.ts` (comment-prose), and its siblings |
| `DEFERRED_SURFACES` declared at `:245` — what it ⛔ does **not** | includes `.changeset/**` **by name** at `:267`, alongside `**/CHANGELOG.md` and `scripts/**` |

⇒ **a bare `#N` on an added line is judged only inside a citation surface.** A diff confined to
`.changeset/`, `scripts/**` or a `CHANGELOG.md` is ⛔ not reachable by that gate. Confirmed independently by
`dispatch-gates`, which omits the family from what it derives for `.changeset/` paths.

### ⚠️ How this seat got it wrong

Four dispatch words this session carried 「it judges **every** bare `#N` on an added line」. On diffs inside
`packages/**/src/**` that is **true**, which is why it survived four rounds; on a `.changeset/`-only diff
(PR #19627) it is **false**, and the dev measured it rather than inheriting it.

### ⭐ Why this belongs beside the other readings on this card, and how it differs

The four errors recorded above are **measurement** failures: a zero reported without the control that proves
the instrument fired. This one is a **recall** failure: a mechanism stated as measured whose **scope** was
never read. The gate's own exclusion list is 55 entries and one grep away.

⇒ **the rule to write down**: a mechanism carried into a dispatch word is a **claim**. Before asserting one,
read the thing's **scope** — the globs, the exclusions, the `--base` it needs — ⛔ not just its behaviour.
Recalling behaviour correctly and asserting it out of scope produces a confident, checkable, wrong
instruction, and a dev that trusts it loses a round for nothing.

## ⛔ Correction to this card's carrier-axis reading — it was missing a precondition, and the missing half is what decides the common case, 2026-09-22T05:10Z

This card carries the seat's platform/gate readings. One of them is wrong in the direction that predicts a **false red**, so it is corrected here before anyone writes it up.

**What this seat has been saying:** the clause-② carrier axis (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1576`) reds `Check Changeset` «only when every moved package is graded `patch`».

⚠️ That is the necessary condition stated as if it were the sufficient one. ⭐ Note the shape of the error: an earlier round already corrected this reading ONCE, by *adding* the all-`patch` condition — and in doing so dropped the precondition that was there before. A correction that replaces one half-rule with another half-rule is the failure mode, not the fix.

**The rule, read from `judgeLevel`'s own docblock rather than recalled:**

| verdict | condition | exit |
|:--|:--|--:|
| `not-declared` | the declaration reads `no` and names **no `narrowing` arm** | **0** |
| `clean` | the axis is **CARRIED**, and no moved package is graded `patch` | 0 |
| `discharged` | the axis is **CARRIED**, and a moved package IS graded `minor`+ | 0 |
| `enforce` | the axis is **CARRIED**, moved packages graded `patch`, **none** at `minor`+ | **1** |

⇒ **`enforce` requires the axis to be CARRIED.** All-`patch` alone never reds it: a bare `Clause-②: no` short-circuits to `not-declared` and **exit 0 before grading is reachable**.

⭐ And the non-obvious half, quoted from the docblock: **«the axis is CARRIED (`yes`, or `no (narrowing)` — the arm carries it too, #16421)»**. A `no` WITH a `narrowing` arm carries the axis exactly as a `yes` does, and the same docblock says `clean`, `discharged` and `enforce` are «every one of them reachable on a `no (narrowing)`». So «declared `no` ⇒ the axis is off» is false too.

**Where it was measured:** PR #19655 declares a bare `Clause-②: no` and grades both moved packages `patch` — the exact shape the old reading predicts as red. `Check Changeset` reads **success**. The corollary worth carrying: that green is *conditional on* the declaration being a bare `no`; had it been `yes`, both-`patch`-with-none-at-`minor` is precisely the `enforce` shape.

**Provenance.** Raised by the at-tier contract reviewer of PR #19655 (record `5771481179`) against a statement in this seat's own review dispatch. ⛔ Not adopted on its word: the ladder above is read from `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` in this act, because this seat has already turned one reading of this gate into an over-general rule once and the remedy for that is to read the source, not to trust a second summary of it.
